import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Create a cleaned breed column to group different sizes of mixed-breed dogs ('Mischling')
# and standardize some common breed names.
df['BreedClean'] = df['Rasse1Text'].astype(str).str.strip()
df.loc[df['BreedClean'].str.contains('Mischling', na=False), 'BreedClean'] = 'Mischling (Mixed Breed)'
df.loc[df['BreedClean'] == 'Franz. Bulldogge', 'BreedClean'] = 'French Bulldog'

# Identify the top 10 most common breeds based on the most recent year's data for relevance
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
top_breeds = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year]['BreedClean'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the dataframe to only include these top breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['BreedClean'].isin(top_breeds)]

# Group by year and breed to get the annual count
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'BreedClean']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# Pivot the data for easier plotting and to handle potential missing year/breed combos
breed_trends_pivot = breed_trends.pivot(index='StichtagDatJahr', columns='BreedClean', values='count')


# --- Visualization ---
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9))

# Use a color palette that is distinct
colors = plt.get_cmap('tab10').colors

# Plot each breed's trend
breed_trends_pivot.plot(
    kind='line',
    ax=ax,
    linewidth=2.5,
    marker='o',
    markersize=5,
    color=colors
)

# --- Customization and Labels ---
ax.set_title(f'Popularity Trends of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich ({df["StichtagDatJahr"].min()}-{latest_year})', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', pad=25)
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Customize ticks and grid
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)
ax.grid(True, which='major', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.6)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True)) # Ensure integer years on x-axis
plt.xticks(rotation=0)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_color('grey')
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('grey')

# Improve the legend
legend = ax.legend(title='Dog Breed', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13)
legend.get_frame().set_alpha(0.95)
legend.get_frame().set_edgecolor('lightgrey')


# Add annotations for the top 5 breeds at the end of the lines for clarity
last_year_data = breed_trends_pivot.iloc[-1].sort_values(ascending=False)
for i, breed in enumerate(last_year_data.index[:5]):
    count = last_year_data[breed]
    line_color = colors[list(breed_trends_pivot.columns).index(breed)]
    ax.text(
        breed_trends_pivot.index[-1] + 0.1,
        count,
        f' {breed}',
        fontsize=11,
        color=line_color,
        verticalalignment='center',
        fontweight='bold'
    )

# Add a source credit
fig.text(1.0, 0.01, 'Source: Open Data Zurich', ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=9, color='#555555', transform=ax.transAxes)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off, accounting for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 0.85, 0.95])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
